# Tail-hedge overlay — report

**Slug:** `family-tail-hedge-overlay`
**Window:** 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29, development only. The 2024-2026
holdout was never loaded, inspected or used.
**Execution:** `research/bt.py`, 1-minute marks, next-open fills, 2% band,
long-only, weights ≥ 0, sum ≤ 1. Headline 1 bp; 5 bp and 10 bp also reported.
**Primary:** 100% TQQQ core; on the first minute close where TQQQ is ≤ −2.0%
from the session open, switch to 50% TQQQ + 50% synthetic inverse TQQQ from the
next minute's open through the next session's open; then re-enter 100% TQQQ.

> **Holdout note:** a `holdout.json` and `holdout_run.log` appeared in this
> directory from a separate process after the development run. This agent did
> not read, inspect or use them. Every number in this report and in
> `result.json` is development-only.

---

## 1. Headline

| cost | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | vol | invested | fills | turnover | ending equity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **1 bp** | **90.84%** | **40.23%** | **1.66** | 2.40 | 45.1% | 100% | **3,985** | 57,321x | **$17,413,571** |
| 5 bp | 76.94% | 46.43% | 1.50 | 2.15 | 45.1% | 100% | 3,971 | 36,560x | $9,520,569 |
| 10 bp | 61.35% | 53.57% | 1.29 | 1.86 | 45.1% | 100% | 3,977 | 21,631x | $4,559,504 |

The `bt.stats` invested fraction is 100% because both TQQQ and the synthetic
inverse are invested assets. The useful exposure split is **mean TQQQ 86.35%,
mean inverse 13.65%, mean BIL 0%**. The inverse is held on **27.3% of bars**;
there are **742 trigger sessions out of 2,012 (36.9%)**. The mean hedge weight
while active is 50%.

Turnover is measured by `bt.py` against the *starting* equity, so it is
inflated by the 174x equity growth. The strategy trades a 50% switch on about
93 sessions per year; that is high, and the 5/10 bp rows show it.

## 2. Direct comparison with `ratio-froth` and the cash control

The cash control is the same trigger and the same 50% hedge, but the hedge
asset is BIL instead of the synthetic inverse.

| variant | cost | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **primary** | **1 bp** | **90.84%** | **40.23%** | **1.66** | 2.40 | 3,985 |
| cash control | 1 bp | 65.41% | 65.81% | 1.24 | 1.77 | 3,133 |
| `ratio-froth` | 1 bp | 61.56% | 39.11% | 1.47 | 2.09 | 619 |
| primary | 5 bp | 76.94% | 46.43% | 1.50 | 2.15 | 3,971 |
| cash control | 5 bp | 53.51% | 69.44% | 1.10 | 1.56 | 3,129 |
| `ratio-froth` | 5 bp | 56.62% | 41.75% | 1.39 | 1.97 | 619 |
| primary | 10 bp | 61.35% | 53.57% | 1.29 | 1.86 | 3,977 |
| cash control | 10 bp | 39.89% | 73.46% | 0.91 | 1.30 | 3,125 |
| `ratio-froth` | 10 bp | 50.67% | 45.03% | 1.28 | 1.82 | 619 |

**Target scorecard:**

| test | result |
|---|---|
| dev CAGR > 61.56% | **yes**, 90.84% |
| dev Sharpe > 1.47 | **yes**, 1.66 |
| dev max DD ≤ 39.11% | **no**, 40.23% (1.1 pp worse) |
| hedge adds CAGR vs cash | **yes**, +25.4 pp |
| hedge reduces DD vs cash | **yes**, −25.6 pp |
| ≥ 100 fills | **yes**, 3,985 |

At 0 bp the primary's DD is **38.95%**, slightly better than ratio-froth's
39.11%; the 1 bp cost adds 1.28 pp. The adjacent **h = 0.50, thr = −1.8%** grid
cell is a strict dominance at 1 bp — **79.55% / 37.68% / 1.56** — but it is not
the primary. The primary is the round 50% / −2.0% cell.

The inverse hedge clearly beats the cash control: the cash control keeps 50%
TQQQ exposure through the tail and therefore keeps a 65.8% drawdown, while the
inverse sleeve neutralises that half. The kill criterion is not met.

## 3. What the hedge actually does

740 episodes, measured from the trigger+1 open to the next session's open
(the actual exit fill).

| statistic | value |
|---|---:|
| episodes | 740 |
| mean TQQQ return over the hedge period | **−0.280%** |
| mean 50/50 portfolio return over the hedge period | **−0.024%** |
| mean log improvement per episode | **+0.364%** |
| total log improvement, 2016-2023 | **+2.695** (≈ +33.7%/yr log) |
| negative-logdiff episodes | **379 (51.2%)** |
| top 10 episodes' share of total logdiff | **63.4%** |
| top 20 episodes' share | **109%** |

The intraday and overnight legs both contribute:

| leg | mean TQQQ | mean 50/50 | mean logdiff |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| intraday (trigger+1 open → 15:59) | −0.181% | −0.013% | +0.232% |
| overnight (15:59 → next open) | −0.087% | +0.000% | +0.145% |

The overnight leg is about **40% of the log edge**. This is why the primary
holds the hedge overnight and exits at the next open. Exiting at 15:59 instead
gives **69.29% / 75.51% / 1.23**; conditioning the overnight hold on a weak
close gives **71.21% / 65.36% / 1.36**. The next-open re-entry is a real part
of the result, not an execution detail.

**By year (sum of episode logdiff):**

| year | n | mean TQQQ | mean 50/50 | sum logdiff |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | 68 | −0.070% | −0.016% | +0.078 |
| 2017 | 41 | +0.156% | +0.005% | −0.048 |
| 2018 | 100 | −0.689% | +0.000% | **+0.800** |
| 2019 | 68 | +0.200% | −0.019% | −0.124 |
| 2020 | 118 | −0.409% | −0.116% | **+0.625** |
| 2021 | 96 | +0.114% | −0.011% | −0.062 |
| 2022 | 156 | −0.819% | −0.005% | **+1.501** |
| 2023 | 93 | +0.124% | −0.004% | −0.076 |

2018 and 2022 together supply about **85%** of the total log edge; 2020 adds
**23%**; the calm years (2017, 2019, 2021, 2023) net negative. This is a
classic tail-hedge profile: many small bleed days, a handful of very large
saves. It is **not** an all-weather alpha.

**Calendar-year returns (primary, 1 bp):**

| year | primary | ratio-froth | cash control |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | +30.2% | +5% | +25% |
| 2017 | +104.9% | +114% | +108% |
| 2018 | **+56.9%** | −2% | +12% |
| 2019 | **+102.5%** | +52% | +117% |
| 2020 | **+311.0%** | +219% | +218% |
| 2021 | +71.7% | +85% | +82% |
| 2022 | **−11.4%** | −19% | −55% |
| 2023 | **+169.6%** | +155% | +191% |

(`ratio-froth` and cash-control years are rounded from the same daily-close
yearly calculation.)

The primary beats ratio-froth in 2016, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2022 and 2023, and
lags 2017 (104.9% vs 114%) and 2021 (71.7% vs 85%). The 2018 and 2022 rows are
the hedge: +56.9% versus −2% in 2018, and −11.4% versus −19% in 2022.

## 4. 8-cell parameter plateau

All cells at 1 bp, 1-minute marks, primary bolded.

| h | −1.6% | −1.8% | −2.0% | −2.2% |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.40 | 63.18 / 52.15 / 1.35 | 73.10 / 44.81 / 1.45 | 81.56 / 51.62 / 1.53 | 79.30 / 57.16 / 1.48 |
| 0.50 | 65.99 / 41.57 / 1.42 | 79.55 / 37.68 / 1.56 | **90.84 / 40.23 / 1.66** | 87.61 / 49.04 / 1.60 |

(values are CAGR / max DD / Sharpe)

**All 8 cells beat 61.56% CAGR.** The CAGR plateau is broad: 63.2% to 90.8%.
The drawdown plateau is narrower: only the h = 0.50 cells at −1.6%, −1.8% and
−2.0% have DD ≤ 41.6%. The h-profile is monotonic — 48.2% at h = 0.10, 60.3% at
h = 0.20, 71.3% at h = 0.30, 81.6% at h = 0.40, 90.8% at h = 0.50 — so the
primary sits at the **50% mandate cap**. h = 0.60-0.75 improves CAGR further
(≈98-106%) but is a net short during the hedge, outside the 10-50% hedge
mandate, and is not used.

## 5. Subperiods

| period | primary CAGR / DD / Sharpe | cash control | ratio-froth |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | **75.76% / 34.75% / 1.68** | 62.95% / 44.50% / 1.39 | 37.07% / 39.11% / 1.13 |
| 2020-2021 | **170.73% / 29.26% / 2.28** | 143.01% / 51.51% / 1.79 | 146.51% / 31.40% / 2.06 |
| 2022-2023 | **58.18% / 38.23% / 1.13** | 15.50% / 62.80% / 0.54 | 45.40% / 24.17% / 1.32 |

The primary beats ratio-froth on CAGR in all three cuts. The 2022-2023 cut is
the weak spot: higher CAGR, but a worse DD (38.23% vs 24.17%) and a worse Sharpe
(1.13 vs 1.32). The 2016-2019 cut is strong, but 2018 Q4 is most of it.

## 6. Placebo / randomized trigger dates

250 full 1-minute backtests per placebo, seeded at 2026.

| placebo | mean CAGR | sd | p95 | max | p(real ≤ placebo) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| random sessions, real bar-offset distribution | 23.89% | 12.14 | 45.44% | 74.84% | **0.00 (0/250)** |
| shifted trigger sessions | 23.84% | 12.05 | 44.60% | 76.84% | **0.00 (0/250)** |
| random sessions at 10:30 | 25.78% | 14.45 | 49.13% | 82.95% | **0.00 (0/250)** |

The real 90.84% is above every one of the 750 placebo draws. The nearest
placebo maximum (82.95%) is still 7.9 pp below the real result, so the signal is
significant but not overwhelmingly separated from the luckiest random draw.

A same-session random-bar placebo is **not** used: it selects sessions using a
future trigger (it knows the session will eventually trigger) and is therefore
not a causal test. In an earlier diagnostic it produced a higher CAGR than the
real strategy, which is exactly the hindsight-selection artifact one expects.

## 7. Idea-space tests

### 7.1 Cash-only control (idea 2)

**65.41% / 65.81% / 1.24** at 1 bp, 3,133 fills. The inverse hedge adds
**+25.4 pp CAGR** and **−25.6 pp DD** versus cash at the same trigger. Kill
criterion not met: the inverse hedge adds both.

### 7.2 Confirmation by QQQ underperformance / trend (idea 3)

| variant | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| no confirmation (primary) | **90.84%** | **40.23%** | **1.66** | 3,985 |
| TQQQ < 3×QQQ (any underperformance) | 67.38% | 62.46% | 1.31 | 3,381 |
| TQQQ < 3×QQQ − 10 bp | 47.90% | 69.99% | 0.98 | 1,335 |
| TQQQ < 3×QQQ − 20 bp | 37.99% | 76.88% | 0.84 | 535 |
| QQQ 3-session return < 0 | 31.48% | 79.80% | 0.78 | 2,123 |
| QQQ above 20-day SMA | 61.32% | 77.97% | 1.09 | 1,909 |
| QQQ 3d < 0 and 20d above SMA | 33.38% | 82.87% | 0.77 | 591 |

Every confirmation filter hurts badly. The best hedges are sudden drops in
otherwise strong markets, not ongoing downtrends or days when TQQQ is already
underperforming 3× QQQ. Breadth data is not in the panel, so QQQ
underperformance was the available proxy; it does not help. The primary uses no
confirmation.

### 7.3 Hedge cost budget (idea 4)

| cap | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| no cap (primary, ~93/yr) | **90.84%** | **40.23%** | **1.66** | 3,985 |
| 180 episodes/year | 90.84% | 40.23% | 1.66 | 3,985 |
| 120 episodes/year | 85.10% | 43.13% | 1.56 | 3,785 |
| 90 episodes/year | 82.90% | 59.61% | 1.49 | 3,365 |
| 60 episodes/year | 59.13% | 70.18% | 1.14 | 2,491 |

A 120-episode/year budget costs 5.7 pp CAGR and 2.9 pp DD; tighter caps fail
the target. The hedge cost is not the binding constraint; the tail events are.
The primary uses no budget.

### 7.4 Overnight-only-when-close-weak (idea 5)

| variant | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| always hold overnight, exit next open (primary) | **90.84%** | **40.23%** | **1.66** |
| hold overnight only when close weak | 71.21% | 65.36% | 1.36 |
| exit at 15:59, no overnight | 69.29% | 75.51% | 1.23 |

The unconditional overnight hold is the best of the three. Conditioning the
overnight hold on a weak close removes the hedge on exactly the days when the
overnight continuation does not look weak at 15:59 but still gaps down.

### 7.5 Trigger-time distribution

Timing is not an opening-only artifact:

| window | episodes | share | mean rest-of-day TQQQ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| first 15 min | 103 | 13.9% | −0.21% |
| first 30 min | 227 | 30.6% | −0.28% |
| first 60 min | 372 | 50.1% | −0.32% |
| after 60 min | 370 | 49.9% | −0.04% |

## 8. Synthetic construction and costs

**Construction:** the hedge asset is a constant-notional −1x TQQQ NAV built
recursively from the same 1-minute bars, rebalanced every minute, with
1.5%/yr net borrow + financing and no short rebate. It is a **synthetic
long-only sleeve**, not a real short: the portfolio never carries a negative
weight. `bt.py` charges slippage on the synthetic notional.

**Borrow sensitivity (1 bp):**

| borrow + financing | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.0%/yr | 91.23% | 40.10% | 1.67 |
| 1.5%/yr (primary) | 90.84% | 40.23% | 1.66 |
| 5.0%/yr | 89.96% | 40.56% | 1.65 |
| 10.0%/yr | 88.75% | 41.12% | 1.64 |

Borrow is not the main cost; the 50% switch and its slippage are.

**Construction variants (1 bp):**

| variant | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| minute-rebalanced inverse TQQQ (primary) | 90.84% | 40.23% | 1.66 |
| daily-reset, no intraday rebalance | 91.66% | 41.84% | 1.67 |
| inverse QQQ instead of inverse TQQQ | 73.38% | 58.88% | 1.39 |

The result is not a minute-rebalancing artifact: the daily-reset version is
slightly better on CAGR and slightly worse on DD. Inverse QQQ is a much weaker
hedge because 50% of a −1x QQQ sleeve only neutralises one-third of the TQQQ
beta.

**Slippage sensitivity:**

| cost | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 bp | 94.58% | 38.95% | 1.71 |
| 1 bp | 90.84% | 40.23% | 1.66 |
| 2 bp | 87.24% | 41.70% | 1.62 |
| 5 bp | 76.94% | 46.43% | 1.50 |
| 10 bp | 61.35% | 53.57% | 1.29 |
| 20 bp | 33.64% | 65.33% | 0.87 |

This is the main practical caveat. The 1 bp headline is the task convention,
but a 50% switch on ~93 sessions per year is a high-turnover implementation.
At 5 bp the strategy still beats ratio-froth on CAGR and Sharpe, but its DD is
46.43% versus 41.75%; at 10 bp the CAGR is 61.35% and the DD is 53.57%. The
advantage is real but cost-sensitive.

## 9. Correlations to `ratio-froth` and the other eight winners

Daily returns over the dev window, n = 2,011 sessions.

| strategy | correlation |
|---|---:|
| `ratio-froth` | 0.596 |
| `vol-scaled-crash-stop` | **0.846** |
| `relative-value-tqqq` | 0.692 |
| `fomc-opex-window` | 0.585 |
| `family-session-timing` | 0.602 |
| `family-short-reversal` | 0.601 |
| `family-rebalance-flow` | 0.709 |
| `family-intraday-microstructure-day` | 0.652 |
| `family-ml-microstructure` | 0.673 |

The strategy is a TQQQ timing overlay, not a diversifying alpha sleeve. Its
highest correlation is with `vol-scaled-crash-stop` (0.846), another
de-risking strategy. The mechanism is different — a crash-contingent inverse
hedge rather than a vol/ATR de-risk — but the return stream is in the same
TQQQ-beta complex.

## 10. Causality and implementation

- All signals use TQQQ closes through the trigger bar; the target fills at the
  **next minute's open**. No signal uses the fill bar's future.
- The synthetic inverse NAV is recursive: `inv_close[t]` depends only on bars
  up to `t`.
- **Pre-cut test:** truncate the panel at 2020-03-12 11:07 ET and rebuild.
  **409,376 bars compared; max abs weight diff = 0.0; max abs synthetic-NAV
  diff = 0.0.** The 11:07 bar is mid-session and cannot change any prior
  target.
- No full-sample normalisation, no trend/vol/drawdown state, no calendar, no
  ML, no relative-strength gate.
- 2% band, 1 bp headline, 5/10 bp reported. Long-only, row sum ≤ 1.
- Deterministic; the only randomness is the seeded placebo (2026).

## 11. Verdict

**Literal target: yes on CAGR and Sharpe; no on drawdown at 1 bp.**

- Higher dev CAGR than `ratio-froth`: **90.84% vs 61.56%**.
- Higher Sharpe: **1.66 vs 1.47**.
- Max DD: **40.23% vs 39.11%**, 1.1 pp worse at 1 bp; **38.95% at 0 bp**,
  slightly better.
- Fills: **3,985**, well above the 100 floor.
- The cash control is clearly worse (**65.41% / 65.81% / 1.24**), so the
  inverse hedge adds both CAGR and DD reduction. The kill criterion is not met.
- The adjacent −1.8% grid cell is a strict dominance
  (**79.55% / 37.68% / 1.56**) but is not the primary.

**What supports the result:**

- The hedge adds +25.4 pp CAGR and −25.6 pp DD versus the cash control at the
  same trigger.
- All 8 grid cells beat 61.56% CAGR; the CAGR plateau is broad.
- The placebo is significant: 0/250 random or shifted draws reach the real
  CAGR.
- The primary beats ratio-froth CAGR in all three subperiods.
- The pre-cut audit is exactly zero.

**What limits the claim:**

1. **Tail concentration.** 2018 and 2022 supply about 85% of the log edge;
   51.2% of hedge episodes lose money; the top 10 episodes supply 63.4%. The
   effective sample is a handful of crash events, not a broad cross-section.
2. **The hedge is at the 50% cap.** The h-profile is monotonic; h = 0.50 is
   the best allowed, not an interior optimum. h = 0.60-0.75 would be a net
   short and is outside the mandate.
3. **Cost sensitivity.** 10 bp CAGR is 61.35% with 53.57% DD; 5 bp is 76.94%
   with 46.43% DD. The 1 bp headline is optimistic for this turnover.
4. **Correlation.** 0.846 to `vol-scaled-crash-stop`; this is a TQQQ timing
   overlay, not a new diversifier.
5. **2022-2023 is the weak cut.** CAGR is higher than ratio-froth, but DD
   (38.23% vs 24.17%) and Sharpe (1.13 vs 1.32) are worse.
6. **Synthetic execution.** The inverse is not a real short; the result
   assumes a constant-notional −1x TQQQ swap with 1.5%/yr borrow and 1 bp
   slippage. Real swap spreads, margin and borrow terms could be worse.

**Honest description:** a crash-contingent 50% inverse TQQQ hedge that truncates
the left tail of a 100% TQQQ core. It beats `ratio-froth` on development CAGR
and Sharpe and is within 1.1 pp of its drawdown at 1 bp. It is not a robust
all-weather strategy: the edge is concentrated in 2018 and 2022, the hedge sits
at the mandate cap, and the result is cost-sensitive. I would keep it as a
strong development result and a genuinely different family mechanism, but I
would not promote it as a validated winner without the 2024-2026 holdout and a
live-implementation cost check.

## 12. Files

- `HYPOTHESIS.md` — mechanism, exact rules, synthetic construction, grid,
  falsifiers.
- `strategy.py` — `build_weights(ts, opens, closes)`, `build_panel(...)` and
  `main()`; writes `result.json`.
- `result.json` — headline windows, cash control, ratio-froth, 8-cell grid,
  confirmation/budget/overnight variants, cost and borrow sensitivity,
  construction variants, subperiods, placebo, correlations, yearly, drawdown
  anatomy, episode study, pre-cut audit.
- `report.md` — this file.
- `robustness.md` — compact tables for the auxiliary tests.

# Tail-hedge overlay — hypothesis

**Slug:** `family-tail-hedge-overlay`
**Window:** 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29, development only. The 2024-2026 holdout
was never loaded, inspected or used.
**Target:** `ratio-froth` dev **61.56% CAGR / 39.11% max DD / 1.47 Sharpe**
(1-minute marks, 1 bp, 2016-01-04..2023-12-29).

> **Holdout note:** a `holdout.json` and `holdout_run.log` appeared in this
> directory from a separate process after the development run. This agent did
> not read, inspect or use them. Every number in this document and in
> `result.json` is development-only.

## Mechanism

A 100% TQQQ core carries a fat left tail: after a fast intraday drawdown, the
sell-off often continues into the close and the next open. A 50% synthetic
inverse TQQQ sleeve, opened only after a −2.0% TQQQ drawdown from the session
open, neutralises the core during that tail. The book re-enters TQQQ at the
next session's open, so it keeps the rebound.

This is a **tail-hedge / convexity overlay**, not a 100-250 day trend gate, not
volatility targeting, not a drawdown-recovery state machine, not a calendar
clock, not an opening-range/close-flow rule, not ML and not relative strength.
The hedge is the primary mechanism; the core is a constant 100% TQQQ.

## Exact rules

1. **Core:** 100% TQQQ at all times when not hedged.
2. **Trigger:** at any minute close of session *d*, if
   `TQQQ_close <= TQQQ_session_open * (1 - 0.020)`, that bar is the trigger.
   Use the first trigger of the session. The target written on the trigger bar
   fills at the **next minute's open**. The trigger uses only bars at or before
   the fill bar.
3. **Hedge:** from that fill, hold **50% TQQQ + 50% synthetic inverse TQQQ**
   for the rest of the session **and overnight**. The 15:59 target is 100%
   TQQQ, so the hedge is exited and the core is re-entered at the next
   session's open.
4. A trigger on the last bar (15:59) is ignored: there is no later bar in the
   session to fill before the overnight re-entry.
5. **No confirmation filter in the primary.** QQQ-underperformance, QQQ
   3-session-negative and QQQ-20-day-SMA filters are tested and rejected
   (section 7 of `report.md`).
6. Weights are long-only, ≥ 0, row sum ≤ 1. Next-open fills, 2% band, 1 bp
   headline, 5/10 bp reported.

## Synthetic inverse TQQQ

The local panel has no inverse ETF. The hedge asset is a **constant-notional
−1x TQQQ NAV** built from the same adjusted 1-minute bars:

```
inv_open[t]  = inv_close[t-1] * (1 - (TQQQ_open[t]  / TQQQ_close[t-1] - 1))
inv_close[t] = inv_open[t]    * (1 - (TQQQ_close[t] / TQQQ_open[t]  - 1)
                                   - cost_per_bar)
```

with `cost_yr = 1.5%/yr` net borrow + financing. The short rebate is ignored,
which is conservative. This is a **synthetic long-only sleeve**, not a real
short position: the portfolio never carries a negative weight. The backtest
holds it as a long asset and `research/bt.py` charges slippage on its traded
notional like any other asset. The result therefore assumes the synthetic can
be implemented as a constant-notional total-return swap or a continuously
rebalanced short. A daily-reset, no-intraday-rebalance variant and a −1x QQQ
variant are reported as robustness checks.

## Why it might work

- After the first −2% trigger, the rest-of-day TQQQ return is negative on
  average: **−0.181% across 740 episodes**, versus **−0.087% overnight**.
- A 50/50 TQQQ/inverse book is nearly flat during the hedge period (mean
  **−0.024%**) while 100% TQQQ loses **−0.280%**. The hedge does not need to
  make money on average; it needs to truncate the left tail. The geometric
  value of avoiding a −10% to −15% day is much larger than the cost of missing
  a +5% rebound.
- Re-entering at the next open is a real part of the result: exiting at 15:59
  (no overnight hedge) cuts CAGR from 90.84% to 69.29% and raises max DD from
  40.23% to 75.51%; conditioning the overnight hold on a weak close gives
  71.21% / 65.36%.
- The inverse's convexity is what turns a −15% TQQQ day into a roughly flat
  portfolio day; the log improvement on those days is what compounds.

## Primary and 8-cell grid

The 8-cell grid is **h ∈ {0.40, 0.50} × thr ∈ {−1.6%, −1.8%, −2.0%, −2.2%}**.
The primary is the round **h = 0.50, thr = −2.0%** cell, **not** the best cell
in the grid. The −1.8% cell is a strict dominance (79.55% / 37.68% / 1.56) but
is not the primary. The grid was fixed before the final run; it is not a blind
pre-registration, because the development window was used for exploration.

## Falsifiers / kill criteria

1. Primary 1 bp CAGR ≤ 61.56% → fail.
2. Primary max DD ≥ 50% → fail.
3. Hedge does not add CAGR versus the cash control → retire.
4. Hedge does not reduce DD versus the cash control → retire.
5. Fewer than 6 of the 8 grid cells above 61.56% CAGR → not a plateau.
6. Placebo p > 0.05 → weak signal.
7. 10 bp CAGR < 61.56% → cost-fragile; report it as such.
8. Pre-cut weight or synthetic-NAV diff > 0 → look-ahead.
9. Fewer than 100 full-window fills → dead/low-fill.

## What would make us retire it

- The inverse hedge's 1 bp CAGR is not above the cash control at the same
  trigger, or its DD is not lower.
- Random trigger dates with the same frequency and timing produce a similar
  CAGR.
- The 5/10 bp results collapse below ratio-froth's 1 bp bar.
- The tail concentration is extreme (top 10 > 80% of the log edge) and the
  sample has fewer than ~10 independent tail events. The current top-10 share
  is **63.4%**, which is high but not disqualifying; the report treats it as a
  major limitation, not as proof of a robust all-weather edge.

the trigger bar fills at the next minute's open.  From that fill the book is

    50% TQQQ + 50% synthetic inverse TQQQ

for the rest of the session *and overnight*.  The 15:59 target is 100% TQQQ,

----------------------

from the same adjusted TQQQ 1-minute bars:

    inv_open[t]  = inv_close[t-1] * (1 - (TQQQ_open[t]  / TQQQ_close[t-1] - 1))
    inv_close[t] = inv_open[t]    * (1 - (TQQQ_close[t] / TQQQ_open[t]  - 1)
                                       - cost_per_bar)

with `cost_yr = 1.5%/yr` (net borrow + financing; the short rebate is ignored,
which is conservative).  This is a *synthetic long-only sleeve*, not a real
short position.  The backtest holds it as a long asset; `research/bt.py`
charges slippage on the traded notional exactly as it does for TQQQ.  The
result therefore depends on the synthetic being implementable as a
constant-notional total-return swap or a continuously rebalanced short.  A
daily-reset, no-intraday-rebalance variant and a -1x QQQ variant are reported
as robustness checks.

---------
`build_weights(ts, opens, closes)` takes the standard QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel and
returns weights in the synthetic panel space

    column 0 = TQQQ, column 1 = synthetic inverse TQQQ, column 2 = BIL.

The primary must therefore be simulated with `build_panel(...)`; see `main()`.
Weights are >= 0, row sum <= 1, next-open fills, 2% band, 1 bp headline and
5/10 bp reported.

Run:

    $env:BT_THREADS = "1"

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402

DEV_START, DEV_END = "2016-01-04", "2023-12-29"
BPY = 252 * 390
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

PARAMS = dict(
    h=0.50,             # hedge fraction of equity (max 50% by mandate)
    thr=-0.020,         # TQQQ drawdown from session open
    cost_yr=0.015,      # synthetic borrow + financing, no short rebate
    hedge_asset=1,      # 1 = synthetic inverse TQQQ, 2 = BIL (cash control)
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# synthetic inverse NAV
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def inverse_nav(opens, closes, cost_yr=0.015, bars_per_year=BPY):
    """Constant-notional -1x NAV from one asset's minute bars.

    Returns (inv_open, inv_close).  The recursion uses only bars up to t, so
    truncating the input produces the same NAV up to the cut.
    """
    o = np.asarray(opens, dtype=float)
    c = np.asarray(closes, dtype=float)
    n = len(o)
    per_bar = float(cost_yr) / bars_per_year
    io = np.empty(n)
    ic = np.empty(n)
    io[0] = 1.0
    ic[0] = 1.0 - (c[0] / o[0] - 1.0) - per_bar
    prev_c, prev_i = c[0], ic[0]
    for t in range(1, n):
        gap = o[t] / prev_c - 1.0
        io[t] = prev_i * (1.0 - gap)
        intra = c[t] / o[t] - 1.0
        ic[t] = io[t] * (1.0 - intra - per_bar)
        prev_c, prev_i = c[t], ic[t]
    return io, ic


def inverse_nav_daily_bounds(opens, closes, first, last, cost_yr=0.015,
                             bars_per_year=BPY):
    o = np.asarray(opens, dtype=float)
    c = np.asarray(closes, dtype=float)
    n = len(o)
    per_bar = float(cost_yr) / bars_per_year
    io = np.empty(n)
    ic = np.empty(n)
    f0, l0 = int(first[0]), int(last[0])
    base0 = 1.0
    for t in range(f0, l0 + 1):
        io[t] = base0 * (1.0 - (o[t] / o[f0] - 1.0))
        ic[t] = base0 * (1.0 - (c[t] / o[f0] - 1.0))
    for k in range(1, len(first)):
        f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
        gap = o[f] / c[int(last[k - 1])] - 1.0
        base = ic[int(last[k - 1])] * (1.0 - gap - per_bar * (l - f + 1))
        for t in range(f, l + 1):
            io[t] = base * (1.0 - (o[t] / o[f] - 1.0))
            ic[t] = base * (1.0 - (c[t] / o[f] - 1.0))
    return io, ic


def build_panel(ts, opens, closes, cost_yr=0.015, kind="minute"):
    """Return the synthetic (n,3) panel [TQQQ, INV, BIL]."""
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    if kind == "minute":
        inv_o, inv_c = inverse_nav(opens[:, 1], closes[:, 1], cost_yr)
    elif kind == "daily":
        inv_o, inv_c = inverse_nav_daily_bounds(
            opens[:, 1], closes[:, 1], first, last, cost_yr)
    else:
        raise ValueError(kind)
    syn_o = np.column_stack([opens[:, 1], inv_o, opens[:, 2]])
    syn_c = np.column_stack([closes[:, 1], inv_c, closes[:, 2]])
    return syn_o, syn_c


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# weights
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_weights(ts, opens, closes, params=None):
    """Return (n,3) weights in the [TQQQ, INV, BIL] synthetic panel space.

    `opens`/`closes` are the standard QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel.  Column 0 is used
    only for the QQQ confirmation diagnostics and column 1 for the TQQQ
    trigger.  The primary hedge asset is column 1 of the synthetic panel.
    """
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    h = float(p["h"])
    thr = float(p["thr"])
    hedge_asset = int(p["hedge_asset"])

    n = len(ts)
    day = bt.day_ids(ts)
    _, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    sess_open_t = opens[first, 1][day]
    ret_from_open = closes[:, 1] / sess_open_t - 1.0

    w = np.zeros((n, 3))
    w[:, 0] = 1.0
    for k in range(1, len(first)):
        f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
        hit = np.flatnonzero(ret_from_open[f:l + 1] <= thr)
        if len(hit) == 0:
            continue
        b = f + int(hit[0])
        # A trigger on the last bar has no later bar in the session to fill
        # before the overnight re-entry; ignore it.
        if b >= l:
            continue
        # Hedge from the next open through the session close, then hold it
        # overnight: the 15:59 target is TQQQ, so the exit fills at the next
        # session's open.
        w[b:l, :] = 0.0
        w[b:l, 0] = 1.0 - h
        w[b:l, hedge_asset] = h
        w[l, :] = 0.0
        w[l, 0] = 1.0
    return w


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# evaluation helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _run(w, ts, opens, closes, slip=1.0, start=DEV_START, end=DEV_END):
    if start == DEV_START and end == DEV_END:
        r = bt.run(ts, opens, closes, w, start, band=0.02,
                   slippage_bps=slip)
    else:
        i = bt.start_index(ts, start)
        j = int(ts.searchsorted(
            pd.Timestamp(end, tz="America/New_York"), side="right"))
        r = bt.simulate(ts[i:j], opens[i:j], closes[i:j], w[i:j],
                        band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
    return r, bt.stats(r, BPY)


def _metrics(w, ts, opens, closes, slip=1.0, start=DEV_START, end=DEV_END):
    r, s = _run(w, ts, opens, closes, slip, start, end)
    return {
        "cagr": s["cagr"], "max_drawdown": s["max_drawdown"],
        "sharpe": s["sharpe"], "sortino": s["sortino"],
        "volatility": s["volatility"], "exposure": s["exposure"],
        "fills": s["fills"], "turnover": s["turnover"],
        "ending_equity": s["ending_equity"], "years": s["years"],
    }


def _daily_returns(result):
    eq = pd.Series(result["equity"], index=result["ts"])
    de = eq.groupby(eq.index.date).last()
    de.index = pd.to_datetime(de.index)
    return de.pct_change().dropna()


def _yearly(result):
    eq = pd.Series(result["equity"], index=result["ts"])
    de = eq.groupby(eq.index.date).last()
    idx = pd.to_datetime(de.index)
    yr = de.groupby(idx.year).last()
    yr0 = de.groupby(idx.year).first()
    return {int(y): {"strategy": float(yr[y] / yr0[y] - 1.0)} for y in yr.index}


def _dd_anatomy(result):
    eq = result["equity"]
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(eq)
    dd = eq / peak - 1.0
    j = int(np.argmin(dd))
    i = int(np.argmax(eq[:j + 1]))
    de = pd.Series(eq, index=result["ts"]).groupby(result["ts"].date).last()
    dpeak = de.cummax()
    ddd = de / dpeak - 1.0
    return {
        "minute_max_drawdown": float(-dd[j]),
        "minute_peak": str(result["ts"][i]),
        "minute_trough": str(result["ts"][j]),
        "daily_close_max_drawdown": float(-ddd.min()),
    }


def _episode_study(ts, opens, closes, w, params=None):
    """Full hedge-period attribution: trigger+1 open -> next session open."""
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    thr = float(p["thr"])
    h = float(p["h"])
    day = bt.day_ids(ts)
    _, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    sess_open_t = opens[first, 1][day]
    ret_from_open = closes[:, 1] / sess_open_t - 1.0
    syn_o, syn_c = build_panel(ts, opens, closes, p["cost_yr"], "minute")
    rows = []
    for k in range(1, len(first)):
        f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
        hit = np.flatnonzero(ret_from_open[f:l + 1] <= thr)
        if len(hit) == 0:
            continue
        b = f + int(hit[0])
        if b >= l:
            continue
        nb = int(first[k + 1]) if k + 1 < len(first) else len(ts) - 1
        tq = syn_o[nb, 0] / syn_o[b + 1, 0] - 1.0  # next open / entry open
        iv = syn_o[nb, 1] / syn_o[b + 1, 1] - 1.0
        port = (1.0 - h) * tq + h * iv
        rows.append((str(bt.session_dates(ts)[l]), b - f, tq, iv, port,
                     float(np.log1p(port) - np.log1p(tq))))
    ep = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["date", "bar", "tqqq", "inv", "port", "logdiff"])
    if len(ep) == 0:
        return {"n": 0}
    ep["year"] = pd.to_datetime(ep["date"]).dt.year
    s = ep.sort_values("logdiff", ascending=False)
    total = float(s["logdiff"].sum())
    top = {str(n): float(s.head(n)["logdiff"].sum()) for n in (1, 5, 10, 20)}
    return {
        "n_episodes": int(len(ep)),
        "mean_tqqq_hedge_period": float(ep["tqqq"].mean()),
        "mean_port_hedge_period": float(ep["port"].mean()),
        "mean_logdiff": float(ep["logdiff"].mean()),
        "sum_logdiff": total,
        "negative_episodes": int((s["logdiff"] < 0).sum()),
        "negative_fraction": float((s["logdiff"] < 0).mean()),
        "top_logdiff_sums": top,
        "top10_share": float(top["10"] / total) if total != 0 else None,
        "by_year": {
            int(y): {
                "n": int(len(g)),
                "mean_tqqq": float(g["tqqq"].mean()),
                "mean_port": float(g["port"].mean()),
                "sum_logdiff": float(g["logdiff"].sum()),
            }
            for y, g in ep.groupby("year")
        },
        "worst_15": [
            {"date": r.date, "bar": int(r.bar), "tqqq": float(r.tqqq),
             "port": float(r.port), "logdiff": float(r.logdiff)}
            for r in ep.nsmallest(15, "tqqq").itertuples()
        ],
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main():
    ts, o0, c0 = bt.panel(("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"), DEV_START, DEV_END, "1min")
    assert ts[-1].date() <= pd.Timestamp(DEV_END).date(), "holdout leaked"
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    nd = len(first)

    syn_o, syn_c = build_panel(ts, o0, c0, PARAMS["cost_yr"], "minute")
    w = build_weights(ts, o0, c0)
    w_cash = build_weights(ts, o0, c0, {"hedge_asset": 2})

    out = {
        "agent": "family-tail-hedge-overlay",
        "family": "tail-hedge / convexity overlay",

    # headline costs
    for slip, lab in ((1.0, "1bp"), (5.0, "5bp"), (10.0, "10bp")):

    for slip, lab in ((1.0, "1bp"), (5.0, "5bp"), (10.0, "10bp")):
        out["cash_control"][lab] = _metrics(w_cash, ts, syn_o, syn_c, slip)

    # benchmarks
    out["benchmarks"]["tqqq_minute"] = bt.benchmark(c0[:, 1], ts, BPY)
    out["benchmarks"]["qqq_minute"] = bt.benchmark(c0[:, 0], ts, BPY)
    out["benchmarks"]["tqqq_note"] = (
        "bt.benchmark on 1-minute marks; the task bar is 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% "
        "max DD / 0.82 Sharpe on daily-close marks.")

    # ratio-froth reference
    import importlib.util
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "ratio_froth", ROOT / "research" / "new" / "ratio-froth" / "strategy.py")
    rf = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(rf)
    w_rf, _ = rf.build_weights(ts, o0, c0)
    for slip, lab in ((1.0, "1bp"), (5.0, "5bp"), (10.0, "10bp")):
        r = bt.run(ts, o0, c0, w_rf, DEV_START, band=0.02,
                   slippage_bps=slip)
        s = bt.stats(r, BPY)
        out["ratio_froth"][lab] = {
            "cagr": s["cagr"], "max_drawdown": s["max_drawdown"],

            "turnover": s["turnover"], "ending_equity": s["ending_equity"],
        }

    # 8-cell plateau
    for h in (0.40, 0.50):
        for thr in (-0.016, -0.018, -0.020, -0.022):
            pp = {"h": h, "thr": thr}
            ww = build_weights(ts, o0, c0, pp)
            m = _metrics(ww, ts, syn_o, syn_c, 1.0)
            out["grid"].append({"name": f"h={h:.2f} thr={thr*100:.1f}%",

    # confirmation variants (idea 3)
    _, _, _ = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    day = bt.day_ids(ts)
    sess_open_t = o0[first, 1][day]
    sess_open_q = o0[first, 0][day]
    ret_t = c0[:, 1] / sess_open_t - 1.0
    ret_q = c0[:, 0] / sess_open_q - 1.0
    qc = c0[last, 0]
    q3 = pd.Series(qc).pct_change(3).to_numpy()
    q20 = pd.Series(qc).rolling(20).mean().to_numpy()

    def build_filtered(thr=-0.020, qqq_under=None, q3_neg=False, q20_up=False,
                       h=0.50):
        n = len(ts)
        ww = np.zeros((n, 3))
        ww[:, 0] = 1.0
        for k in range(1, nd):
            f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
            cond = ret_t[f:l + 1] <= thr
            if qqq_under is not None:
                cond &= ret_t[f:l + 1] < 3.0 * ret_q[f:l + 1] - qqq_under
            if q3_neg:
                cond &= np.isfinite(q3[k - 1]) and q3[k - 1] < 0
            if q20_up:
                cond &= np.isfinite(q20[k - 1]) and qc[k - 1] > q20[k - 1]
            hit = np.flatnonzero(cond)
            if len(hit) == 0:
                continue
            b = f + int(hit[0])
            if b >= l:
                continue
            ww[b:l, :] = 0.0
            ww[b:l, 0] = 1.0 - h
            ww[b:l, 1] = h
            ww[l, :] = 0.0
            ww[l, 0] = 1.0
        return ww

    for name, kwargs in (
        ("no_confirmation_primary", {}),
        ("tqqq_worse_than_3x_qqq", {"qqq_under": 0.0}),
        ("tqqq_worse_than_3x_qqq_minus_10bp", {"qqq_under": 0.001}),
        ("tqqq_worse_than_3x_qqq_minus_20bp", {"qqq_under": 0.002}),
        ("qqq_3session_return_negative", {"q3_neg": True}),
        ("qqq_above_20d_sma", {"q20_up": True}),
        ("qqq_3d_negative_and_20d_up", {"q3_neg": True, "q20_up": True}),
    ):
        ww = build_filtered(**kwargs)
        out["confirmation_variants"][name] = _metrics(
            ww, ts, syn_o, syn_c, 1.0)

    # budget variants (idea 4): cap the number of hedges per calendar year
    def build_budget(max_episodes):
        n = len(ts)
        ww = np.zeros((n, 3))
        ww[:, 0] = 1.0
        used = {}
        for k in range(1, nd):
            f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
            hit = np.flatnonzero(ret_t[f:l + 1] <= PARAMS["thr"])
            if len(hit) == 0:
                continue
            b = f + int(hit[0])
            if b >= l:
                continue
            yr = dates[l].year
            if used.get(yr, 0) >= max_episodes:
                continue
            used[yr] = used.get(yr, 0) + 1
            ww[b:l, :] = 0.0
            ww[b:l, 0] = 1.0 - PARAMS["h"]
            ww[b:l, 1] = PARAMS["h"]
            ww[l, :] = 0.0
            ww[l, 0] = 1.0
        return ww

    for cap in (60, 90, 120, 180):
        out["budget_variants"][f"max_{cap}_per_year"] = _metrics(
            build_budget(cap), ts, syn_o, syn_c, 1.0)

    # overnight variants (idea 5)
    lo = np.minimum.reduceat(c0[:, 1], first)[day]
    hi = np.maximum.reduceat(c0[:, 1], first)[day]
    close_pos = (c0[:, 1] - lo) / np.maximum(hi - lo, 1e-9)

    def build_exit(mode="weak_only", h=0.50, thr=-0.020, weak_close=0.3):
        n = len(ts)
        ww = np.zeros((n, 3))
        ww[:, 0] = 1.0
        for k in range(1, nd):
            f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
            hit = np.flatnonzero(ret_t[f:l + 1] <= thr)
            if len(hit) == 0:
                continue
            b = f + int(hit[0])
            if b >= l:
                continue
            if mode == "always_overnight":
                end = l
            elif mode == "weak_only":
                weak = c0[l, 1] < o0[f, 1] or close_pos[l] < weak_close
                end = l if weak else l - 1
            elif mode == "close":
                end = l - 1
            else:
                raise ValueError(mode)
            ww[b:end, :] = 0.0
            ww[b:end, 0] = 1.0 - h
            ww[b:end, 1] = h
            ww[end:l + 1, :] = 0.0
            ww[end:l + 1, 0] = 1.0
        return ww

    for name, mode in (("always_overnight_primary", "always_overnight"),
                       ("weak_close_only_overnight", "weak_only"),
                       ("exit_at_1559_no_overnight", "close")):
        out["overnight_variants"][name] = _metrics(
            build_exit(mode=mode), ts, syn_o, syn_c, 1.0)

    # cost sensitivity already in windows; keep a compact 0/2bp table too
    for slip in (0.0, 2.0):
        out["cost_sensitivity"][f"{slip:.0f}bp"] = _metrics(
            w, ts, syn_o, syn_c, slip)
    out["cost_sensitivity"]["note"] = (
        "1/5/10 bp are in windows; 0 and 2 bp show the slope. The strategy is "
        "cost-sensitive because it trades a 50% switch on ~93 sessions/year.")

    # borrow cost sensitivity
    for cost in (0.0, 0.015, 0.05, 0.10):
        so, sc = build_panel(ts, o0, c0, cost, "minute")
        out["borrow_sensitivity"][f"{cost*100:.1f}%/yr"] = _metrics(
            w, ts, so, sc, 1.0)

    # construction variants
    so_d, sc_d = build_panel(ts, o0, c0, PARAMS["cost_yr"], "daily")
    out["construction_variants"]["daily_reset_no_intraday"] = _metrics(
        w, ts, so_d, sc_d, 1.0)
    # inverse QQQ instead of inverse TQQQ
    invq_o, invq_c = inverse_nav(o0[:, 0], c0[:, 0], PARAMS["cost_yr"])
    q_o = np.column_stack([o0[:, 1], invq_o, o0[:, 2]])
    q_c = np.column_stack([c0[:, 1], invq_c, c0[:, 2]])
    out["construction_variants"]["inverse_qqq"] = _metrics(
        w, ts, q_o, q_c, 1.0)

    # subperiods
    for name, a, bnd in (("2016-2019", "2016-01-04", "2019-12-31"),
                         ("2020-2021", "2020-01-02", "2021-12-31"),
                         ("2022-2023", "2022-01-03", "2023-12-29")):
        out["subperiods"][name] = {
            "primary": _metrics(w, ts, syn_o, syn_c, 1.0, a, bnd),
            "cash_control": _metrics(w_cash, ts, syn_o, syn_c, 1.0, a, bnd),
            "ratio_froth": _metrics(w_rf, ts, o0, c0, 1.0, a, bnd),
        }

    # placebo: random trigger dates and shifted dates
    rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
    real_sessions, real_bars = [], []
    for k in range(1, nd):
        f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
        hit = np.flatnonzero(ret_t[f:l + 1] <= PARAMS["thr"])
        if len(hit):
            real_sessions.append(k)
            real_bars.append(int(hit[0]))
    real_sessions = np.array(real_sessions)
    real_bars = np.array(real_bars)
    n_sig = len(real_sessions)

    def build_sessions(session_ids, bar_offsets):
        n = len(ts)
        ww = np.zeros((n, 3))
        ww[:, 0] = 1.0
        for k, off in zip(session_ids, bar_offsets):
            f, l = int(first[k]), int(last[k])
            b = f + int(off)
            if b >= l:
                continue
            ww[b:l, :] = 0.0
            ww[b:l, 0] = 1.0 - PARAMS["h"]
            ww[b:l, 1] = PARAMS["h"]
            ww[l, :] = 0.0
            ww[l, 0] = 1.0
        return ww

    real_cagr = out["windows"]["dev"]["1bp"]["cagr"]

    def summarize(vals):
        a = np.asarray(vals, dtype=float)
        return {
            "n_draws": int(len(a)),
            "mean_cagr": float(a.mean()),
            "std_cagr": float(a.std(ddof=1)),
            "p95_cagr": float(np.quantile(a, 0.95)),
            "max_cagr": float(a.max()),
            "p_value": float((a >= real_cagr).mean()),
        }

    n_draws = 250
    rand_cagr = []
    for _ in range(n_draws):
        kk = rng.choice(np.arange(1, nd - 1), n_sig, replace=False)
        bb = rng.choice(real_bars, n_sig, replace=True)
        ww = build_sessions(kk, bb)
        _, ss = _run(ww, ts, syn_o, syn_c, 1.0)
        rand_cagr.append(ss["cagr"])
    shift_cagr = []
    for _ in range(n_draws):
        sh = int(rng.integers(1, nd - 1))
        kk = ((real_sessions - 1 + sh) % (nd - 2)) + 1
        ww = build_sessions(kk, real_bars)
        _, ss = _run(ww, ts, syn_o, syn_c, 1.0)
        shift_cagr.append(ss["cagr"])
    t1030 = int(np.flatnonzero(
        ts[first[1]:last[1] + 1].strftime("%H:%M") == "10:30")[0])
    fixed_cagr = []
    for _ in range(n_draws):
        kk = rng.choice(np.arange(1, nd - 1), n_sig, replace=False)
        ww = build_sessions(kk, np.full(n_sig, t1030))
        _, ss = _run(ww, ts, syn_o, syn_c, 1.0)
        fixed_cagr.append(ss["cagr"])
    out["placebo"] = {
        "real_cagr": real_cagr,
        "real_trigger_sessions": int(n_sig),
        "real_trigger_share_of_sessions": float(n_sig / nd),
        "random_sessions_real_bar_offsets": summarize(rand_cagr),
        "shifted_sessions": summarize(shift_cagr),
        "random_sessions_1030_bar": summarize(fixed_cagr),
        "note": "Random and shifted placebos preserve the number of triggers "
                "and (for the random-session draw) the intraday bar-offset "
                "distribution. A same-session random-bar placebo is not used: "
                "it selects sessions using a future trigger and is therefore "
                "not causal.",
    }

    # correlations vs ratio-froth and the other eight winners
    r1 = _run(w, ts, syn_o, syn_c, 1.0)[0]
    rs = _daily_returns(r1)
    curve_dir = ROOT / "research" / "new" / "curves"
    winners = ["ratio-froth", "vol-scaled-crash-stop", "relative-value-tqqq",
               "fomc-opex-window", "family-session-timing",
               "family-short-reversal", "family-rebalance-flow",
               "family-intraday-microstructure-day", "family-ml-microstructure"]
    for slug in winners:
        p = curve_dir / f"{slug}.json"
        if not p.exists():
            out["correlations"][slug] = None
            continue
        d = json.load(open(p))
        q = pd.Series(d["values"], index=pd.to_datetime(d["dates"]))
        q = q.pct_change().dropna()
        j = rs.index.intersection(q.index)
        out["correlations"][slug] = {
            "n": int(len(j)),
            "corr": float(np.corrcoef(rs.loc[j], q.loc[j])[0, 1]),
        }

    # yearly and drawdown anatomy
    out["yearly"] = _yearly(r1)
    out["dd_anatomy"] = _dd_anatomy(r1)
    out["episode_study"] = _episode_study(ts, o0, c0, w)

    # weights / exposure diagnostics
    out["weights"] = {
        "mean_tqqq": float(w[:, 0].mean()),
        "mean_inverse": float(w[:, 1].mean()),
        "mean_bil": float(w[:, 2].mean()),
        "bars_with_inverse": float((w[:, 1] > 0).mean()),
        "trigger_sessions": int(n_sig),
        "trigger_share": float(n_sig / nd),
        "note": "bt.stats exposure is 1.0 because TQQQ and the synthetic "
                "inverse are both invested assets; the TQQQ/inverse split is "
                "the relevant exposure.",
    }

    # pre-cut causality: truncate at 2020-03-12 11:07 and compare prior weights
    cut = int(ts.searchsorted(
        pd.Timestamp("2020-03-12 11:07", tz="America/New_York")))
    pre = bt.start_index(ts, "2020-03-12")
    w_cut = build_weights(ts[:cut], o0[:cut], c0[:cut])
    inv_cut_o, inv_cut_c = inverse_nav(o0[:cut, 1], c0[:cut, 1],
                                       PARAMS["cost_yr"])
    out["precut"] = {
        "cut": "2020-03-12 11:07 America/New_York",
        "bars_compared": int(pre),
        "max_abs_weight_diff": float(np.max(np.abs(
            w_cut[:pre, 1] - w[:pre, 1]))),
        "max_abs_inverse_nav_diff": float(np.max(np.abs(
            inv_cut_c[:pre] - syn_c[:pre, 1]))),
        "note": "all weights and the synthetic NAV through the 2020-03-11 "
                "15:59 close are identical; the 11:07 cut is mid-session and "
                "cannot change any prior target.",
    }

    dev = out["windows"]["dev"]["1bp"]
    out["status"] = (
        "dev_pass" if (dev["cagr"] > 0.6156 and dev["max_drawdown"] < 0.50)
        else "dev_fail")
    out["kill_criteria"] = {
        "hedge_adds_cagr_vs_cash": bool(
            dev["cagr"] > out["cash_control"]["1bp"]["cagr"]),
        "hedge_reduces_dd_vs_cash": bool(
            dev["max_drawdown"] < out["cash_control"]["1bp"]["max_drawdown"]),
        "beats_ratio_froth_cagr": bool(
            dev["cagr"] > out["ratio_froth"]["1bp"]["cagr"]),
        "beats_ratio_froth_sharpe": bool(
            dev["sharpe"] > out["ratio_froth"]["1bp"]["sharpe"]),
        "no_worse_ratio_froth_dd": bool(
            dev["max_drawdown"] <= out["ratio_froth"]["1bp"]["max_drawdown"]),
    }

    (OUT / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, default=float))
    print(json.dumps({
        "status": out["status"],
        "windows": out["windows"]["dev"],
        "cash_control": out["cash_control"]["1bp"],
        "ratio_froth": out["ratio_froth"]["1bp"],
        "kill_criteria": out["kill_criteria"],
        "placebo": out["placebo"],
        "dd_anatomy": out["dd_anatomy"],
        "weights": out["weights"],
    }, indent=2, default=float))
    print("wrote", OUT / "result.json")
